title: Swe mid scenario cascading failure
question: One downstream service your API depends on starts responding slowly, and now your whole API is timing out for unrelated requests too. What's happening, and how would you prevent it?
idealAnswer:
Identifies the mechanism: slow calls to the downstream service are tying up request threads/connections, so the pool gets exhausted and even requests that don't need that service get stuck waiting

Proposes a timeout on the downstream call itself, currently it's likely calling with no timeout or an overly generous one, letting slow calls hang indefinitely

Proposes a circuit breaker pattern, after enough failures/timeouts, stop calling the downstream service for a cooldown period and fail fast instead of piling up more stuck requests

Recognizes the deeper design issue: calling the dependency synchronously and unconditionally on every request when only some requests need it, and suggests making it optional, async, or cached where possible

Bonus: mentions bulkheading, isolating resources (e.g. separate thread/connection pools) per downstream dependency so one slow dependency can't exhaust resources needed for unrelated requests
